Department_Program: Bogen International Graduate Program, Dept of Economics (direct PhD)
Format: Full-time only, 5 yrs (2 coursework + 3 research). English-taught.
Funding_Summary: Merit scholarships + travel/visit support; tuition normally waived. Stipend figure not published. Competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Victor Lavy (development/education econ, field + quasi-experimental methods)
Advantages: Best-in-class impact-evaluation training in exactly his methods; direct-from-BA entry possible; same ecosystem as HUJI Business School finance + Milken Innovation Center.
Disadvantages: Pure economics: no securitization/tranching expertise in-house; full-time only, coursework-heavy; GRE required.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low-moderate: no part-time path; Israel pilot on the doorstep but full-time academic culture.
Verification_Status: Supervisor verified (method fit); finance side needs co-advisor
Fit_Notes: Local pilot access; strongest methods training in Israel but least venture-friendly and light on finance-structuring.

Department_Program: Coller School of Management, Doctoral Program (Finance)
Format: Full-time research model, up to 5 yrs; English available (TAU International).
Funding_Summary: TAU PhD stipends for full-time students (progress-contingent); tuition normally waived. Coller-specific figure unverified.
Key_Supervisors: Danny Ben-Shahar (housing/household finance, mortgage + credit markets); Sivan Frenkel (contracts, information econ, financial regulation)
Advantages: Top Israeli management school; deep finance bench for pricing/tranching/securitization mechanics; Ben-Shahar anchors the lending-analytics layer; Tel Aviv = centre of migrant-worker population.
Disadvantages: No published development-finance/microfinance/impact-eval specialist (needs econ co-advisor from Berglas); GMAT-quant or psychometric required; thesis master's expected; venture tolerance undocumented.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Moderate: excellent Tel Aviv pilot proximity; finance-academic culture less obviously venture-flexible.
Verification_Status: Supervisor verified (finance); pair with Berglas econ
Fit_Notes: Sustainability + finance interdisciplinary. Excellent for the finance-engineering half; needs an economics co-advisor for impact evaluation.

Department_Program: Dept of Public Policy & Management / Dept of Economics
Format: Research (thesis) PhD track; format/language not fully published. Likely more Hebrew-centric.
Funding_Summary: Standard Israeli PhD funding/fellowships; lower cost of living. Figures unverified.
Key_Supervisors: Ofer Azar (behavioral economics) - not development finance; policy supervisors To identify
Advantages: Policy framing; potentially strong funding vs cost of living; social-policy specialization aligns with the development-impact angle.
Disadvantages: No verified microfinance/securitization/impact-eval supervisor; likely more Hebrew; farther from the central-Israel migrant-worker pilot.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Uncertain: part-time unverified; geographically less convenient for a central-Israel pilot.
Verification_Status: Supervisor to verify - contact department first
Fit_Notes: Development and behavioral economics. Plausible policy home but unproven supervisor fit; pursue only after confirming an advisor.

Department_Program: Jerusalem School of Business Administration, PhD (Finance / Risk)
Format: Full-time, phased (~2+2+2.5 yrs); flexible supervisor-built curriculum (only ~12 mandatory credits). Outside PART-TIME employment explicitly permitted (no full employment).
Funding_Summary: School + research-foundation scholarships plus TA income (progress/excellence-contingent). Fee coverage not published. Competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Orly Sade (financial inclusion, financial literacy, fintech, household finance); Yishay Yafeh (banking, emerging markets; Milken Innovation Center); Anat Bracha (behavioral econ, poverty; IPA affiliate)
Advantages: Single best supervisor-and-topic match in Israel; flexible research-led structure; outside part-time work allowed (most venture-tolerant funded route); plugged into Milken blended-finance lab + IPA RCT network.
Disadvantages: Effectively requires a master's; stipend size + English-track PhD supervision must be confirmed in writing; cannot combine with full employment.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High (for Israel): flexible structure, outside part-time work permitted, Israel pilot local, practitioner-linked supervisors.
Verification_Status: Supervisor verified (strong); confirm English track + stipend
Fit_Notes: NEW route distinct from Bogen. The standout Israeli option on supervisor fit and venture tolerance.

Department_Program: Eitan Berglas School of Economics (Economics PhD)
Format: Full-time, up to 5 yrs; standard (from MA) or direct (from BA) track; substantial coursework. English info provided.
Funding_Summary: Full-time PhD stipends for 4 yrs (progress-contingent); tuition normally waived. Competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Analia Schlosser (labor + development econ, immigration; quasi-experimental/field methods; IZA/CEPR)
Advantages: Rigorous development/applied-micro training; funded; Schlosser a genuine impact-evaluation fit; natural co-advising with Coller finance.
Disadvantages: Heavy coursework, full-time, least venture-flexible TAU route; no securitization/finance-structuring in-house.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low-moderate (full-time, coursework-heavy) but excellent Tel Aviv pilot proximity.
Fit_Notes: The rigorous impact-evaluation anchor at TAU; pair with Coller finance for the structuring side.

Department_Program: Faculty of Data & Decision Sciences (PhD)
Format: Multiple tracks ~3.5-5 yrs; English track available; supervisor-first admission.
Funding_Summary: Best-documented funding here: tuition-exempt + monthly scholarship ~NIS 6,000-6,500+/mo, plus excellence awards.
Key_Supervisors: Quantitative finance / operations research / decision-science faculty (structuring, risk, monitoring). Development/impact specialist To identify.
Advantages: Clear, generous, documented funding; English track; strong quantitative methods for the structuring engine (tranching, first-loss, monitoring ops).
Disadvantages: Engineering/quant faculty: no development-econ/microfinance/impact-eval specialist; Haifa-based (farther from central-Israel pilot).
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Moderate: strong funding but full-time; venture-parallel tolerance unverified.
Verification_Status: Program verified; topical supervisor to verify
Fit_Notes: Best-funded, strongest on quantitative risk/structuring methods; only if he reframes toward the analytics/decision-science core.

Department_Program: Oxford Sustainable Finance Group, via DPhil Geography & the Environment
Format: Direct DPhil (no compulsory MRes), 3-4 yrs full-time; residency-heavy. No standalone Smith School DPhil - OSFG supervises via SoGE.
Funding_Summary: Clarendon Fund + ESRC Grand Union DTP cover fees+stipend, open to internationals but extremely competitive. No OSFG-specific stipend advertised.
Key_Supervisors: Ben Caldecott (sustainable finance, stranded assets, climate/nature risk) - Director OSFG
Advantages: World-leading sustainable-finance brand and convening power; strong for the securitizable green/impact-asset framing; Clarendon open to internationals.
Disadvantages: DPhil sits in Geography, not finance - structured-finance + RCT-econometrics supervision must be sourced elsewhere; residency clashes with venture; funding fierce; no named community-lending/microinsurance supervisor.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Moderate-low: prestigious and on-theme but full-time residency and a geography base make parallel venture + field RCTs harder.
Fit_Notes: High-prestige, high-theme, structurally awkward and funding-competitive; best only if Caldecott/OSFG actively want the topic.

Department_Program: MRes/PhD Finance (also MRes/PhD International Development)
Format: 2-yr MRes + 3-4-yr PhD, full-time; part-time only in limited circumstances. Finance route GRE/GMAT-gated.
Funding_Summary: LSE + ESRC (LISS-DTP) + departmental scholarships, open to home + overseas but very competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Deep finance + development-econ + impact-eval benches; specific community-lending/microinsurance supervisor To identify (do not assume).
Advantages: Best-in-class impact-evaluation + finance-theory methods; the International Development MRes/PhD route is more fieldwork/venture-tolerant while keeping LSE econometrics.
Disadvantages: Finance route coursework-heavy, full-time, GRE-gated, not venture-designed; overseas funding scarce; securitization craft not an LSE Finance signature.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Finance route low; International Development route moderate.
Fit_Notes: Deep risk + development finance expertise. The International Development door is the more venture-compatible LSE route.

Department_Program: Judge Business School PhD (Finance pathway); CISL is master's-only
Format: 9-month MPhil/MRes + 4-yr PhD, full-time, coursework-heavy, residency-based. CISL offers NO PhD.
Funding_Summary: Strong: Judge guarantees maintenance at research-council rate (approx GBP 20,285 for 2024/25) + fees yrs 1-3; Cambridge Trust/Gates/college awards; shortfall covered.
Key_Supervisors: Finance faculty lean corporate finance/asset pricing/fintech; Elroy Dimson (responsible investing) NOT available as principal supervisor. Topic match weak.
Advantages: Best UK funding certainty of the shortlist; Cambridge brand; strong finance methods.
Disadvantages: Weak named supervisor fit for community-lending securitization; full-time, coursework-heavy, residency-based; CISL cannot host the PhD.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low.
Verification_Status: Program verified; supervisor fit is the weak link
Fit_Notes: Quant finance + sustainability network. Best funding certainty but topical supervision is the risk - pursue only if a Judge finance professor bites.

Department_Program: Sustainable Development, Economic Growth & Finance PhD (Business School)
Format: PhD, 3 yrs FT / 6 yrs PT, October start.
Funding_Summary: This advertised opportunity is SELF-FUNDED (UK ~GBP 5,238/yr; intl ~GBP 23,100/yr). Separate funded studentships advertised individually. 2026 deadline (31 Jul) has passed - expect reopening.
Key_Supervisors: No named supervisor on listing; theme covers financial inclusion, green finance, climate risk, inclusive growth. Contact To identify.
Advantages: Explicitly inclusive-finance-friendly theme (closest stated scope to his question); part-time route available; lower-pressure entry than Oxbridge/LSE.
Disadvantages: Advertised route self-funded; no named supervisor confirmed; less structured-finance depth than a specialist finance school.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Good: part-time route + applied/inclusive-finance theme.
Verification_Status: Program verified; supervisor + funding to secure
Fit_Notes: Financial systems + inclusive growth focus. Flexible and thematically welcoming but likely self-funded unless a separate studentship is landed.

Department_Program: MPhil/PhD Development Economics; Centre for Sustainable Finance / Centre for Global Finance
Format: MPhil upgrading to PhD; 3 yrs +1 FT or 6 yrs +1 PART-TIME (on-campus London, not distance).
Funding_Summary: Home fee ~GBP 5,055; intl ~GBP 23,390. ESRC (Bloomsbury DTP), Felix (developing-country nationals), SOAS Teaching, Tibawi. Intl funding competitive; self-fund often the default.
Key_Supervisors: Ulrich Volz (development/sustainable/climate finance, financial-market development; Director, SOAS Centre for Sustainable Finance)
Advantages: Arguably the strongest UK thematic home for development finance + financial inclusion + sustainable finance in one place; part-time route; Felix/DTP funding; regional strengths fit migrant-worker + African field sites.
Disadvantages: Lighter on hard structured-finance/tranching technique and quant asset pricing than a finance school; intl funding competitive; part-time still needs London presence.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High: part-time route, fieldwork-native; but periodic London presence needed.
Fit_Notes: Top-tier thematic + supervisor fit, part-time-friendly. Pair with a structured-finance mentor.

Department_Program: Global Development Institute (PhD); Alliance MBS for finance co-supervision
Format: PhD 3-4 yrs FT; part-time available; proposal-driven, supervisor-first.
Funding_Summary: ESRC NWSSDTP + President's Doctoral Scholar awards (intl-eligible, competitive); GDI funds few per year.
Key_Supervisors: Kunal Sen (development econ, growth); Antonio Savoia (development finance, governance); Dereje Regasa (financial development, banking); Armando Barrientos (social protection - insurance/safety-net angle)
Advantages: Genuine development-finance + social-protection cluster with named, sourced fits; strong impact-evaluation + fieldwork culture; large DTP; African field sites core.
Disadvantages: Development-studies, not a finance faculty - tranching/securitization needs an Alliance MBS co-supervisor; intl funding competitive.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High: fieldwork-native, part-time possible, African sites core.
Fit_Notes: Excellent development-finance/social-protection supervision with real named fits; add a finance co-supervisor for the securitization craft.

Department_Program: School of Global Development (PhD)
Format: PhD 3-4 yrs; part-time available; proposal-driven.
Funding_Summary: SeNSS DTP studentships cover fees for BOTH UK and international students + stipend (genuinely intl-friendly DTP); January deadlines; competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Arjan Verschoor (field/lab experiments on risk, agricultural investment and weather-index insurance in Uganda - RCT + microinsurance core)
Advantages: Possibly the single best UK methodological supervisor fit for microinsurance + experimental impact evaluation; intl-eligible DTP funding; part-time possible; African fieldwork standard.
Disadvantages: Development-studies base - securitization/tranching needs a finance co-supervisor; smaller finance footprint.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High: fieldwork-native, RCT culture, African sites standard.
Fit_Notes: Outstanding fit for the insurance + RCT core, with international-eligible funding. A top pick; pair with structured-finance input.

Department_Program: Centre for Development Studies (Dept of Social & Policy Sciences), PhD
Format: PhD FT/PT available; proposal-driven. Confirm exact CDS PhD entry page.
Funding_Summary: SWDTP (ESRC South West DTP) studentships, intl-eligible but competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Susan Johnson (financial inclusion + microfinance; long ties to FSD Kenya)
Advantages: Rare named fit on financial inclusion in African contexts with real practitioner (FSD Kenya) ties - very close to the African field-site plan; part-time route possible.
Disadvantages: Development-studies base (not finance) - securitization technique needs a co-supervisor; confirm Johnson's current supervising availability + exact PhD route/URL.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High.
Fit_Notes: Strong supervisor fit on financial inclusion in Africa; pursue if she is available to supervise.

Department_Program: ICMA Centre (Henley Business School), PhD in Finance
Format: Full-time only, 3-4 yrs, September start.
Funding_Summary: Henley/ICMA departmental scholarships, regional bursaries, Felix (developing-country nationals). Funded seats limited.
Key_Supervisors: Lisa Schopohl (programme director). Capital-markets/derivatives/structured-products school; community-lending topic supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Real structured-finance/securitization/market-microstructure technique - the strongest of the pure-finance homes for the tranching craft; Felix funding for developing-country nationals.
Disadvantages: Full-time only (venture-unfriendly); development/impact-evaluation is not ICMA's strength; community-lending supervisor unverified.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low-moderate (FT only).
Verification_Status: Program verified; best as securitization co-supervision
Fit_Notes: Best of the pure-finance options for the securitization craft, but weak on development/impact side and full-time only.

University: Bayes Business School (City St George's, University of London)
Department_Program: Faculty of Actuarial Science & Insurance, PhD / Executive PhD
Format: PhD full-time; also an Executive PhD in Actuarial Science (part-time, fee-paying, practitioner-oriented).
Funding_Summary: Bayes PhD studentships limited/competitive; Executive PhD is self-funded.
Key_Supervisors: Ioannis Kyriakou (actuarial finance). UK-leading insurance/actuarial faculty; named microinsurance/index-insurance supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Best UK actuarial/insurance faculty for the microinsurance pricing/underwriting/first-loss layer; the part-time Executive PhD is unusually venture-compatible.
Disadvantages: Weak on development-economics/impact-evaluation and African fieldwork; standard PhD funding limited; Executive PhD self-funded.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Executive PhD high; standard PhD moderate.
Verification_Status: Program verified; strong as actuarial co-supervision
Fit_Notes: The home for the actuarial/insurance-structuring dimension; strongest as a co-supervision partner or via the part-time Executive route.

University: Institute of Development Studies / University of Sussex
Department_Program: PhD by Research (degree awarded by Sussex)
Format: 3-4 yrs FT; 8 yrs PT but UK RESIDENTS ONLY (intl students cannot do PT on a student visa).
Funding_Summary: No direct IDS/Sussex funding; ESRC SEDarc/SeNSS DTP routes. Intl PT barred.
Key_Supervisors: Historic financial-inclusion/social-protection strength but currently-accepting supervisors rotate; verify a matched, available supervisor (do not assume).
Advantages: World-leading development-studies brand; deep social-protection/financial-inclusion heritage; values field experience.
Disadvantages: No in-house funding; part-time closed to international students; current advertised supervisors do not match; light on structured finance.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Moderate-high for UK residents; reduced if PT needed as an international student.
Fit_Notes: Strong thematic home only if UK-resident and a matched supervisor is confirmed.

Department_Program: PhD in Finance with Swiss Finance Institute (GFRI/GSEM)
Format: Full-time, ~4-5 yrs (1 coursework + 3 research); English. Funded via SFI fellowship or assistantship. No part-time.
Funding_Summary: Tuition only CHF 500/semester; fellowship/assistantship covers living (high Swiss stipends). Very competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Bernd Balkenhol (Professor of Micro-Finance, GFRI; ex-ILO Social Finance - EMERITUS, confirm capacity); Catalina Martinez Gutierrez (impact investing); Giuseppe Ugazio (behavioral philanthropy)
Advantages: Elite finance training + a genuine microfinance chair and impact-investing lecturer; near-zero tuition + funded; Geneva hub for development finance/impact investing/ILO.
Disadvantages: No part-time; demanding first coursework year; a finance PhD - RCT/field-experiment supervision thinner; Balkenhol emeritus; very competitive quant bar.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Medium: excellent theme + network, but full-time coursework-heavy early on.
Fit_Notes: Highly quantitative sustainable finance. Strong on theme, funding and network; best if he can commit full-time.

University: IESEG School of Management / KU Leuven / University of Lille
Department_Program: Joint IESEG-KU Leuven Doctoral Program in Business Economics; or Lille (SESAM) route
Format: Joint: full-time, 4 yrs, FULLY FUNDED, salaried Teaching/Research Assistant, no tuition; ~100 teaching hrs/yr; English. Lille route 3-5 yrs, funding project-dependent. No part-time.
Funding_Summary: Salaried assistant contract (or scholarship), competitive, no fees - one of the cleaner funding propositions.
Key_Supervisors: IESEG via LEM lab; on-topic microfinance supervisor at IESEG To identify. KU Leuven side offers Bert D'Espallier (microfinance) - confirm he can co-supervise on this track.
Advantages: Salaried, fee-free, English; dual French-Belgian brand; publication-oriented; Paris/Lille workable for European venture activity.
Disadvantages: Full-time salaried assistant + teaching load competes with venture time; thematic fit hinges on securing an on-topic supervisor; business-economics framing may favour archival over field RCTs.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Medium: funded + English but teaching duties and full-time status constrain parallel work.
Verification_Status: Program verified; supervisor to secure (D'Espallier via KUL)
Fit_Notes: Applied focus. Attractive funding/structure; verify a genuinely on-topic co-promotor before ranking above Geneva.

University: Universite libre de Bruxelles / Universite de Mons (CERMi)
Department_Program: Centre for European Research in Microfinance (CERMi); PhD via ULB/UMONS doctoral schools
Format: PhD ~4 yrs, English-capable; often salaried research positions or FNRS/FRESH fellowships. CERMi periodically advertises doctoral fellowships.
Funding_Summary: Belgian funded-PhD models (salaried positions / FNRS fellowships) available; fellowship/position-dependent - timing matters.
Key_Supervisors: Marek Hudon (microfinance ethics, social enterprise); Ariane Szafarz (microfinance, gender/discrimination in lending, asset mgmt); Marc Labie (microfinance, financial inclusion); Hubert Tchakoute-Tchuigoua (loan contracts, credit risk, CSR in microfinance)
Advantages: The single most on-topic research home in Europe for microfinance/financial inclusion/social finance - matches VSLA/microinsurance structuring, mission-drift, credit-risk and securitization questions; deep microfinance-industry ties (ADA Luxembourg, European Microfinance Programme).
Disadvantages: Funding fellowship/position-dependent (not guaranteed cohort intake); more economics/management-of-microfinance than securitization engineering (bring the tranching layer yourself); dual-institution admin.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High thematically (venture IS the thesis); Belgian networks reach African microfinance sites; full-time positions still constrain time.
Fit_Notes: Best-in-class supervisor and thematic fit in Europe. Priority target - approach Hudon/Szafarz/Labie about a securitization-focused thesis.

Department_Program: Centre for Finance and Development (CFD); PhD in International Economics
Format: PhD in International Economics (development-heavy); English; scholarships competitive; Swiss cost base.
Funding_Summary: Scholarships available (competitive), not a guaranteed salaried post; high Swiss living costs. Confirm package.
Key_Supervisors: Lore Vandewalle (field experiments/RCTs on financial inclusion, self-help groups, microfinance); Ugo Panizza (development finance, sovereign debt); Nathan Sussman (international finance)
Advantages: Vandewalle is one of the best individual supervisor matches on the whole list (RCTs + financial inclusion); CFD's impact-investing/development-finance framing fits the private-capital-mobilization thesis precisely; Geneva ecosystem (UN, multilaterals, impact funds) ideal for pilots.
Disadvantages: Funding scholarship-competitive; high Swiss living costs; full-time (part-time not standard).
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High (network + methods).
Fit_Notes: Top-tier individual match. Add to shortlist; approach Vandewalle/Panizza directly.

Department_Program: Faculty of Economics and Business (PhD)
Format: Dutch PhDs commonly salaried employee positions (~4 yrs) - funding advantage; English. Entry position-dependent.
Funding_Summary: Salaried-PhD model (must match a funded vacancy or bring funding). Strong funding structure.
Key_Supervisors: Robert Lensink (development finance; microfinance + microinsurance + RCT impact evaluation; J-PAL affiliate)
Advantages: Salaried-PhD model; Lensink combines microfinance + microinsurance + RCTs - nearly exact methodological fit for the verification-heavy design.
Disadvantages: Entry is vacancy/position-dependent; full-time; securitization technique still needs a finance angle.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High methodologically; full-time.
Fit_Notes: Very strong on supervisor fit. Pursue Lensink directly.

Department_Program: Institute of Development Policy (IOB), PhD in Development Studies
Format: PhD (monograph or article-based) + doctoral training; must secure an IOB supervisor before applying; English.
Funding_Summary: Not automatic: Belgian salaried positions / VLIR-UOS / FWO fellowships where available; some self/externally funded. Verify route early.
Key_Supervisors: Danny Cassimon (development finance / finance-for-development, innovative financing mechanisms, debt sustainability, real options for development financing)
Advantages: Cassimon a genuine development-finance/blended-finance supervisor - strong fit for mobilizing private capital + structuring; development-studies framing welcomes impact/RCT and policy relevance.
Disadvantages: Funding not guaranteed (self-source or win a fellowship); fewer pure structured-finance specialists.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Good: policy-relevance requirement rewards an applied venture; African fieldwork core IOB territory.
Fit_Notes: Strong secondary target on the development-finance structuring layer; confirm funding early.

Department_Program: Faculty of Economics & Business / LICOS (PhD in Economics)
Format: Funded PhD positions via annual FEB call; Belgian salaried/fellowship models; ~4 yrs; English.
Funding_Summary: Funded positions (competitive annual call). Salaried/fellowship.
Key_Supervisors: Bert D'Espallier (microfinance institutions, performance, inclusion; CERMi network); LICOS for development/institutional economics
Advantages: Microfinance supervisor + top-ranked economics department + funded positions; also the KU Leuven side of the IESEG joint route (potential co-supervision).
Disadvantages: Competitive funded-position entry; confirm D'Espallier's current supervision availability.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Medium-high.
Fit_Notes: Strong microfinance supervisor within a top department; natural complement to the IESEG joint route.

Department_Program: Doctoral Program (Finance / Economics)
Format: Full-time, up to 5 yrs; English; 100% time commitment. No part-time.
Funding_Summary: Fully funded via Foundation Doctoral Scholarship up to EUR 2,320/mo tax-exempt from yr 1 + research/travel budgets; competitive.
Key_Supervisors: Deep institutional microfinance/financial-inclusion heritage sits in the Advisory Services arm, not necessarily the academic PhD faculty - named academic supervisor To identify (verify before applying).
Advantages: Fully funded, English, finance-rigorous, in a major financial centre; the microfinance/financial-inclusion consulting network is unmatched for practitioner ties + potential pilot partners.
Disadvantages: Full-time 100%-commitment scholarship (hard to run a venture); academic microfinance chair unconfirmed - heritage is advisory, not necessarily supervision.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Medium: excellent network, demanding time commitment.
Verification_Status: Program verified; academic supervisor to verify
Fit_Notes: Strong funding + practitioner network; confirm an on-topic academic supervisor exists before ranking highly.

Department_Program: PhD in Innovation, Economics, Governance & Sustainable Development
Format: Two tracks: (a) full-time 4-yr; (b) 'Dual Career' PhD for working professionals with limited on-site presence + online support (the part-time/venture-parallel option). English.
Funding_Summary: Full-time funding via grants/scholarships (not guaranteed by program; ~10 fellowships in past cycles). Dual Career track typically self/employer-funded.
Key_Supervisors: Distinguished development-economics/impact-evaluation faculty; on-topic financial-inclusion/RCT supervisor To identify (verify).
Advantages: The Dual Career track is a rare explicit part-time/venture-parallel route; UN affiliation + SDG framing fit the development-impact and capital-mobilization narrative.
Disadvantages: Full-time funding not automatic; Dual Career usually self-funded; finance-structuring specialization thin.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High: Dual Career format is purpose-built for professionals running parallel work.
Verification_Status: Program verified (part-time track); supervisor to verify
Fit_Notes: Best structural match for part-time/venture-parallel study; confirm funding + a financial-inclusion/RCT supervisor.

Department_Program: Development Economics Group (PhD)
Format: Dutch salaried-PhD model common (~4 yrs); also externally/sandwich-funded PhDs; English.
Funding_Summary: Salaried-PhD potential (position-dependent).
Key_Supervisors: Erwin Bulte (development econ; field experiments/RCTs, risk, insurance, resilience; IGC/CEPR/ATAI-adjacent)
Advantages: RCT-heavy group; agricultural/rural-finance + index-insurance expertise fits the microinsurance and African-field-site angle; salaried-PhD potential.
Disadvantages: More agricultural/rural development than structured finance; entry position-dependent.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High for African rural pilots + insurance evaluation.
Fit_Notes: Strong for the impact-evaluation + microinsurance side; verify a named funded position.

Department_Program: Centre for Studies and Research on International Development (PhD)
Format: PhD via doctoral college, ~3 yrs; funded doctoral contracts (salaried) awarded competitively; some admin in French; English supervision per supervisor.
Funding_Summary: Fully funded doctoral contracts (contrats doctoraux), competitive annual selection.
Key_Supervisors: Large development-economics faculty (development financing, Sub-Saharan Africa focus); named microfinance/microinsurance supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Funded salaried contracts; one of Europe's heavyweight development-economics centres; deep African-fieldwork + impact-evaluation tradition.
Disadvantages: Competitive fixed-cycle funded-contract entry; some administration in French; supervisor fit unverified.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Good for the African field site; full-time contract limits parallel time.
Fit_Notes: Strong development-economics + African focus + funding; verify a named on-topic supervisor.

Department_Program: Economics PhD (with ZEW research)
Format: Top-tier economics PhD, typically funded; English.
Funding_Summary: Funded (competitive); German structured-PhD norms.
Key_Supervisors: Ralph de Haas (ZEW; also EBRD Director of Research, KU Leuven) - leading development-finance / financial-inclusion scholar
Advantages: Top-tier economics PhD + a leading development-finance supervisor (de Haas) with EBRD ties - strong for the capital-mobilization + banking angle.
Disadvantages: Very competitive; confirm de Haas supervising availability given multiple affiliations; more empirical banking than securitization engineering.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Medium (full-time).
Fit_Notes: Strong development-finance supervisor within a top department; approach de Haas directly.

University: Krea University (IFMR Graduate School of Business)
Department_Program: PhD in Management + affiliated LEAD at Krea (financial inclusion/RCT centre)
Format: BOTH full-time (4 yrs, +1) and PART-TIME (hybrid: in-person + hybrid lectures, on-campus exams). English.
Funding_Summary: Full-time: tuition waiver + monthly stipend + conference funding. Part-time: self-funded.
Key_Supervisors: Jyoti Prasad Mukhopadhyay (PhD chair; development/financial-services econ); LEAD at Krea - Sharon Buteau (financial inclusion, enterprise growth); Financial Well-being & Social Protection research vertical
Advantages: The heartland of Indian financial-inclusion research; LEAD does exactly the RCT/impact-evaluation work the project needs; part-time route exists; genuine field access.
Disadvantages: Part-time self-funded; less global brand prestige than NUS/HKUST; securitization/structured-finance depth thinner (partner with a finance advisor).
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Moderate-high via the part-time hybrid track (periodic India presence for exams, not continuous relocation).
Fit_Notes: Strongest topical + methodological fit in Asia, with a rare part-time option. Top direct-inquiry target.

Department_Program: Lee Kong Chian School of Business, PhD (Finance); also SMU-PHBS DBA in Economics (part-time)
Format: Full-time PhD (stipend + fees); plus a part-time/executive SMU-PHBS DBA in Economics (with Peking Univ HSBC BS). English.
Funding_Summary: PhD funded (SMU norm); DBA self-funded/executive.
Key_Supervisors: Hao Liang (sustainable finance, impact investing, 'Globalization and Affordability of Microfinance'; co-director Singapore Green Finance Centre)
Advantages: Arguably the best-sourced individual supervisor match in Asia (microfinance + sustainable finance + impact investing); Singapore hub; both a research PhD and an executive DBA route exist.
Disadvantages: PhD full-time on-campus (relocation); DBA is a professional degree (practice-weighted credibility).
Venture_Pilot_Fit: PhD low (relocation); DBA moderate.
Fit_Notes: Highest supervisor fit in Singapore. Worth a direct approach to Prof. Liang regardless of program route.

Department_Program: NUS Business School, Dept of Finance; NUS Sustainable & Green Finance Institute (SGFIN)
Format: Full-time, on-campus, ~4-5 yrs; English; GMAT/GRE optional.
Funding_Summary: Full scholarship (tuition + living) + conference/overseas-research funding. Strongly funded.
Key_Supervisors: Johan Sulaeman (Director SGFIN; sustainability/impact measurement in finance). Microfinance/VSLA-specific supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Singapore green-finance hub; strong funding; sustainable finance an explicit departmental theme; SGFIN gives a structuring/impact-measurement home.
Disadvantages: Full-time on-campus (incompatible with running the venture from Israel); technique-heavy (asset pricing), may not centre development/RCT; on-topic supervisor unconfirmed.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low (relocation required).
Fit_Notes: Elite and well-funded, but a full relocation with imperfect topical supervisor fit.

Department_Program: Nanyang Business School, Finance; Centre for Sustainable Finance Innovation + Insurance Risk & Finance Research Centre
Format: Full-time PhD, ~4-5 yrs; English; GMAT/GRE.
Funding_Summary: NTU research scholarships (stipend + tuition for admitted PhDs).
Key_Supervisors: Chang Xin 'Simba' (Director CSFI; sustainable/corporate finance); Jun-Koo Kang (Director, Insurance Risk & Finance Research Centre - the insurance leg); Hong Ru (credit/development-adjacent finance)
Advantages: A dedicated sustainable-finance centre PLUS an insurance-risk centre - an unusually good structural match for lending + microinsurance securitization; strong funding.
Disadvantages: Full-time, relocation; microfinance/RCT development-field angle not the centre's core (leans corporate ESG).
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low (relocation).
Fit_Notes: One of the better thematic matches in Asia (finance + insurance + sustainability), but relocation-bound.

University: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Department_Program: Department of Finance (PhD)
Format: Full-time PhD, ~4 yrs; English; GMAT/GRE; HKPFS application ~1 Dec.
Funding_Summary: Among the most generous globally: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme HK$340,800/yr (~US$43,730) x4 + HK$14,200/yr travel + full tuition waiver; HKUST RedBird top-ups.
Key_Supervisors: Darwin Choi (socially responsible investing); Zhanhui Chen (asset pricing linked to insurance, fintech, sustainable finance); Chu Zhang (financial markets/institutions). No verified microfinance/development-field specialist.
Advantages: Exceptional funding; top-ranked finance department; ESG/green-finance + insurance-adjacent supervisors.
Disadvantages: Full-time relocation + HK student visa; very quantitative, thin on RCT/development-field methods; VSLA supervisor not confirmed.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low (relocation).
Verification_Status: Program + funding verified; topical supervisor to verify
Fit_Notes: Best funding + prestige in Asia, but methodologically distant from the RCT/development core and relocation-bound. (HKU/CUHK/CityU are HKPFS-eligible leads with the same tradeoff.)

University: BRAC University (joint with SOAS, University of London)
Department_Program: Joint PhD in Global Development
Format: Joint PhD in Global Development (SOAS-BRAC). Confirm FT/PT + residency split. English.
Funding_Summary: Confirm - joint programs sometimes carry studentships; assume competitive/partly self-funded until verified.
Key_Supervisors: BRAC (birthplace of large-scale microfinance) field ecosystem + SOAS development-economics supervision. Named supervisors To identify.
Advantages: Best-in-world microfinance field ecosystem (BRAC's own microfinance operations) paired with a UK-degree development-economics supervision.
Disadvantages: New program; funding/format need confirmation; Bangladesh residency component.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Distinctive for the South-Asian/African field-site leg; residency component.
Verification_Status: Program verified; funding + supervisors to verify
Fit_Notes: High-relevance option for the field-site leg; worth a direct enquiry.

Department_Program: Open University Business School, PhD (Accounting & Finance / Economics)
Format: FT (Milton Keynes) and PT. CAVEAT: research-degree PT students 'normally resident in the UK and attend regular meetings' - verify overseas PT eligibility (the make-or-break question).
Funding_Summary: Fully-funded FT studentships via ESRC Grand Union DTP; PT is self-funded.
Key_Supervisors: Departments include Accounting & Finance and Public Leadership & Social Enterprise; named supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Genuine PhD; distance-friendly institutional culture; funded FT route exists.
Disadvantages: PT normally UK-resident (key blocker for an Israel-based applicant) - confirm overseas eligibility first.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Potentially high IF overseas PT permitted; otherwise low.
Verification_Status: Overseas PT residency rule to verify (decisive)
Fit_Notes: Attractive on paper for a remote PhD; hinges entirely on the UK-residency question.

Department_Program: DBA (Doctor of Business Administration)
Format: Fully online / distance-capable, part-time professional research doctorate (DBA, not PhD).
Funding_Summary: Self-funded (DBA norm). Cost/duration not published - request from EBS.
Key_Supervisors: Not listed; EBS is a reputable UK degree-awarding institution (higher credibility than most online DBAs). Supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Genuinely remote - the best pure-distance fit for staying in Israel; UK university with real degree-awarding powers.
Disadvantages: DBA (practice-weighted, not academic-career grade); self-funded; supervisor-on-topic unverified; less RCT methodological depth than a research PhD.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High (fully online, part-time).
Fit_Notes: Leading fully-remote option if a DBA's credibility tradeoff is acceptable.

Department_Program: DBA (also a separate full-time academic PhD in Management)
Format: Part-time blended DBA, 4 yrs (2 coursework + 2 dissertation); only 3 residency periods in Spain (2 weeks each); English. Triple-accredited.
Funding_Summary: Self-funded (fees not published - request from admissions).
Key_Supervisors: Not named on page; IE is AACSB/EQUIS/AMBA triple-accredited (high DBA credibility). Supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Only ~6 weeks total on-site over 4 years - very venture-compatible; strong brand; English.
Disadvantages: Executive-level entry expectation; DBA credibility tier (below a research PhD); self-funded.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High.
Fit_Notes: Among the most travel-light credible DBAs; note the separate full-time PhD in Management if he wants the academic track.

Department_Program: DBA (Doctor of Business Administration)
Format: Part-time, hybrid, 4-6 yrs; DBA (not PhD); English. Triple-accredited.
Funding_Summary: Self-funded: ~GBP 14,500/yr (yrs 1-3), GBP 11,500 (yr 4), GBP 7,500 (yrs 5-6).
Key_Supervisors: Ruth Sealy (programme director); Finance & Accounting research area exists. Supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Prestigious, triple-accredited; hybrid (limited residency); a Finance & Accounting research theme.
Disadvantages: Requires minimum 5 yrs managerial experience; some Henley/Johannesburg presence; DBA (practice-framed); self-funded.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: High (part-time hybrid, executive-oriented).
Fit_Notes: Strong credible-DBA option if the work-experience bar is met and periodic UK/SA presence is workable.

Department_Program: School of Economics / CREDIT (PhD Economics)
Format: PhD (MRes+PhD or direct with strong master's); FT (PT possible - confirm).
Funding_Summary: Midlands Graduate School ESRC DTP; Nottingham studentships; intl-eligible but limited.
Key_Supervisors: Oliver Morrissey (development econ; development finance, aid, trade, fiscal policy). Microfinance/impact co-supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Established development-economics centre (CREDIT); solid econometrics.
Disadvantages: Less on securitization + microinsurance specifically; intl funding competitive.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Moderate.
Fit_Notes: Credible development-economics home; a supporting option rather than a lead.

University: Toulouse School of Economics / Paris School of Economics
Department_Program: Economics PhD (development / contract theory / RCTs)
Format: Elite funded economics PhDs, English; funded doctoral contracts.
Funding_Summary: Funded (competitive); French doctoral contracts salaried.
Key_Supervisors: Strong development + contract-theory (TSE) and development-economics/RCT clusters (PSE, J-PAL Europe ties). Named supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Top-tier economics training + funding; PSE especially strong for impact evaluation.
Disadvantages: Very competitive; no verified microfinance-specialized supervisor yet; full-time.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Low-moderate (full-time).
Fit_Notes: Elite economics + impact-evaluation homes; confirm a development/finance supervisor.

University: University of Gothenburg / Stockholm School of Economics
Department_Program: Economics PhD (Environment for Development / SITE) - Nordic salaried model
Format: Salaried PhD employee positions (~5 yrs, strong funding advantage); English; competitive annual intake.
Funding_Summary: Fully salaried Nordic PhD (best funding model).
Key_Supervisors: Environmental + development economics, RCT/field capacity (EfD network; SITE at SSE). On-topic financial-inclusion supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Fully salaried; development + environmental/climate-finance angle fits the sustainability dimension.
Disadvantages: Finance-structuring thin; microfinance-specific supervisor unverified; relocation to Sweden.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Medium (full-time, salaried).
Verification_Status: Funding model strong; supervisor to verify
Fit_Notes: Excellent funding model + climate/development-economics fit; verify a supervisor.

Department_Program: International Institute of Social Studies, PhD
Format: 4-yr doctorate, largely SELF-FUNDED (must prove funds); English.
Funding_Summary: Self-funded: tuition ~EUR 8,000/yr; total incl. living/fieldwork ~EUR 92,750. Waiver possible on request.
Key_Supervisors: Development-studies strength (social/political economy of development); finance/microfinance supervisor To identify.
Advantages: Development-studies depth; fieldwork-oriented; The Hague policy hub.
Disadvantages: Self-funded model is the weakest funding fit here; finance-structuring expertise unverified.
Venture_Pilot_Fit: Good fieldwork orientation; cost is a real drawback.
Fit_Notes: Thematically credible on development, but the self-funded structure works against the funding priority.
